text:
Alex: Heads-up — during a deploy we noticed a KMS grant to service-account@redwood-prod but there is no corresponding audit log entry in our org/cloud audit logs for an IAM binding change. Anyone else seeing this?
Maya: Huh, which key and when? :eyes:
Alex: key: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/payment/cryptoKeys/charges. Approx time from deploy logs: 2026-03-12T14:22:31Z.
Jon: I checked admin activity for `SetIamPolicy` and `UpdateCryptoKey` around that time — nothing obvious for that resource. Was this via our infra pipeline or manual?
Alex: Our infra logs show a terraform apply by `automation@infra-bot` at 14:22:30Z but terraform state doesn't show any iam_binding change for that key. Snippet: ```[2026-03-12T14:22:30Z] infra-bot: terraform apply finished: changed=3 resources```
Maya: There are two ways to grant access to keys: IAM policy on the cryptoKey and a CryptoKey IAM member or a KMS policy change. Could be `projects.locations.keyRings.cryptoKeys.patch` or a cloud console action that didn't route through terraform. Check Cloud Console audit and admin.googleapis.com/activity.
Jon: I also looked at the KMS API logs exported to BigQuery — no `projects.locations.keyRings.cryptoKeys.setIamPolicy` for that key in that window.
Tara: pinging infra/SRE: @oncall-sre can you pull org-level admin activity and token issuer audit for 14:15-14:30Z? We need the raw proto logs, not just aggregated views.
oncall-sre: Logged. I'll run an org export and grep for `cryptoKeys/charges` and `service-account@redwood-prod`. Creating INC-20351 for tracking.
deploy-bot: Incident INC-20351 created: "missing-kms-audit-event" — oncall notified.
Maya: Action items: (1) Jon — run org export for 2026-03-12T14:15:00Z to 14:30:00Z and grep `cryptoKeys/charges`. (2) Alex — attach terraform plan/state and infra-bot run logs. (3) Tara — verify which tokens had org-level scopes that could bypass normal audit flows.
Jon: Taking the org export now. Also will check if any service principals used an external auth flow (OIDC) that might appear under a different principalName.
Alex: I'll gather infra-bot audit and the deploy run metadata. Noting that if the change came from an internal admin console action, the UI sometimes surfaces under a different project-level principal — we should correlate `protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail` with our SSO records.
Tara: If we still can't find an audit entry, escalate to security lead and GCP support — missing audit trails for KMS is a compliance blocker. Keep updates in this thread.
Maya: Thanks — please copy any export links here. We should be ready to rotate the key if we confirm an unauthorized grant.
